# Notation {#sec-appa}

The notation index connects the symbols in an equation to their meanings and their first matching use. Read the meaning before following the code name: a familiar letter need not represent the same physical quantity in another model. Acronyms and YAML keys, with each concept's defining section, are in the glossary (@sec-apph).

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Find definitions and their supporting chapter evidence.

**Data.** Symbol definitions, units and code names; generated navigation tables.

**Placement.** Report preparation, outside the solver.

**Activation.** Run `gen_notation_index.py`; no solver switch.

**Guarantee / limits.** Index membership does not establish correctness.

**Evidence.** The checks below verify generation against its inputs.
:::

Local symbols: this guide introduces no mathematical variables. Symbols in the tables retain the definitions in their source chapters.

## Why the index is structured this way

1. Read the symbol and its meaning together. The generator copies these cells from the notation table; it does not infer physical dimensions from code.
2. Read the units column. `split_units` extracts a bracketed unit or a count; an empty cell is not evidence of a dimensionless quantity.
3. Follow “first used” to the chapter. `first_use` searches normalized mathematics in book order, so another spelling can give no match even when the concept is present.
4. Follow the chapter's code citation at the code pin before changing an implementation. The index's code column is a copied name, not a fresh source audit.

These operations parse strings and count rows with Python integers. They perform no floating-point reduction;
there is no accumulated round-off term to bound. Exact regeneration tests the rendering contract, not a physical tolerance.

## Conventions at a glance {#sec-appa-conventions}

These tables summarize the tensor layout, row meanings and coordinate conventions at the code pin.
S marks a sourced statement; I marks an inference from the cited source.

### Where things are in a tensor

| # | convention | what to know | source | tag |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | axis order | The hydrodynamic state shape is (variable, $x_3$, $x_2$, $x_1$), with $x_1$ last. For a contiguous tensor, this makes a vertical column contiguous in memory (inference from the layout). | `initialize_local` checks `{nvar, nc3, nc2, nc1}`: [meshblock.cpp#L431-L435](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L431-L435) | S |
| 2 | variable rows | `IDN`=0 density, `IVX`,`IVY`,`IVZ`=1,2,3 velocity (primitive) or momentum (conserved), `IPR`=4 pressure (primitive) or total energy (conserved), `ICY`=5 first species. | [snap.h#L34-L41](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/snap.h#L34-L41) | S |
| 3 | the legacy layout is refused | Species must start right after the five hydro rows; `NMASS > 0` does not compile. | [snap.h#L50-L55](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/snap.h#L50-L55) | S |
| 4 | `IVX` is the $x_1$ (vertical) component | The comment says "X-velocity", but gravity `grav1` acts on row `IVX`. | [snap.h#L37](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/snap.h#L37); [const_gravity.cpp#L48-L51](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/forcing/const_gravity.cpp#L48-L51) | S |
| 5 | ghost cells | Cells per axis = `nx + 2*nghost` if `nx > 1`, else 1. A one-cell axis has no ghosts. | [coordinate.hpp#L63-L65](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/coord/coordinate.hpp#L63-L65) | S |
| 6 | `nghost` default | 1 when the card does not set `cells/nghost`. Many schemes need more; see @sec-ch04. | [coordinate.cpp#L213](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/coord/coordinate.cpp#L213) | S |
| 7 | interior index range | $x_1$ interior is `il = nghost` … `iu = nghost + nx1 - 1` (0 on a one-cell axis). | [coordinate.hpp#L194-L198](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/coord/coordinate.hpp#L194-L198) | S |

### Units and signs

| # | convention | what to know | source | tag |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 12 | SI units | The molar mass is in kg/mol (`weight`, default 29e-3). Specific heats are in J/(kg K). The gas constant is in J/(mol K) (kintera). The examples build $R_d$ = `Rgas / weight`, so $p=\rho R_d T$ is in Pa with $\rho$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$ and $T$ in K. | [equation_of_state.hpp#L47](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/eos/equation_of_state.hpp#L47); [#L104-L115](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/eos/equation_of_state.hpp#L104-L115); kintera `Rgas = 8.31446 // J/(mol*K)` at the kintera commit the book cites, [chengcli/kintera@c55b13b2/src/constants.h#L6](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/c55b13b2204997d2d09e04498558ab9495d8ee77/src/constants.h#L6); [straka.cpp#L69](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/examples/straka.cpp#L69) | S |
| 14 | gravity sign | `grav1` is the $x_1$ acceleration added to momentum and energy: `du[IVX] += dt*rho*grav1`. **Downward is `grav1 < 0`** (the decks use `grav1: -9.8`). The default is 0, meaning no gravity. The unit is m s$^{-2}$ (SI, row 12). | [const_gravity.cpp#L22](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/forcing/const_gravity.cpp#L22), [#L48-L51](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/forcing/const_gravity.cpp#L48-L51); [straka_single.yaml#L58](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/examples/straka_single.yaml#L58) | S |
| 15 | **the opposite sign elsewhere** | `balance_column(grav=…)` and the Straka initial condition take a **positive** downward magnitude: the example writes `grav = -grav1`. | [balance_column.cpp#L18](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/hydro/balance_column.cpp#L18); [straka.cpp#L62](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/examples/straka.cpp#L62) | S |
| 16 | angles given in units of $\pi$ | `x2min_pi` / `x2max_pi` / `x3min_pi` / `x3max_pi` are multiplied by $\pi$; the plain keys are taken as given. | [coordinate.cpp#L81-L84](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/coord/coordinate.cpp#L81-L84) | S |

### Covariant and contravariant components

| # | convention | what to know | source | tag |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 17 | primitive velocity vs stored momentum | The primitive velocity is contravariant. The conserved momentum is $\rho v$ lowered with `coord_vec_lower_`, so it is covariant. | [ideal_gas.cpp#L74-L78](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/eos/ideal_gas.cpp#L74-L78); [coord_utils_impl.h#L18-L24](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/coord/coord_utils_impl.h#L18-L24) | S |
| 18 | only on the cubed sphere does it matter | The lowering uses the cell cosine `cosine_cell_kj`. That is zero on Cartesian and spherical-polar grids, so there momentum is simply $\rho v$. It is $-xy/(CD)$ on the gnomonic panels, where it mixes $x_2$ and $x_3$. | [cartesian.cpp#L12-L14](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/coord/cartesian.cpp#L12-L14); [spherical_polar.cpp#L52-L53](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp#L52-L53); [gnomonic_equiangle.cpp#L77](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/coord/gnomonic_equiangle.cpp#L77) | S |
| 19 | spherical-polar velocity components are physical ($\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$) | **Inference from the cited source:** the radial geometric source is $\rho\,(v_2^2+v_3^2)$ times the area-over-volume factor. That is the form for orthonormal (physical) components. | [spherical_polar.cpp#L244](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp#L244) | I |

### The vertical coordinate

| # | convention | what to know | source | tag |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20 | no pressure, sigma or hybrid coordinate | The only grid types are `cartesian` (the default), `cylindrical`, `spherical-polar` and `gnomonic-equiangle`. Any other name is refused. | [coordinate.cpp#L796-L805](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/coord/coordinate.cpp#L796-L805); default [#L71](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/coord/coordinate.cpp#L71) | S |
| 21 | what it is instead | $x_1$ is a fixed geometric height (Cartesian, in m) or radius (spherical-polar: `x1v` is built by `radial_centers`). Pressure is part of the primitive state on that grid, not a coordinate. **The index $i$ increases upward**: the faces run from `x1min` to `x1max`, so `il` is the bottom cell and `iu` the top one (gravity points to $-x_1$, row 14). | [spherical_polar.cpp#L61](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp#L61); [coordinate.cpp#L466-L469](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/coord/coordinate.cpp#L466-L469); rows 2 and 14 | S |
| 22 | $x_2$ on a spherical-polar grid is the colatitude $\theta$ | The metric uses `sin(x2)` of the $x_2$ faces. | [spherical_polar.cpp#L83-L86](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp#L83-L86) | S |

## How to use and refresh the index {#sec-appa-refresh}

There is no simulation YAML for this appendix: neither generator configures snapy. The generators, their inputs
and the report's checks live in the *report directory*, `doc/tech-report` on the `tech-report` branch of
`UCzhangxi/snapy`. A clone of `chengcli/snapy`, the repository the code citations point to, does not have them. Get
the report directory with

```bash
git clone -b tech-report https://github.com/UCzhangxi/snapy && cd snapy/doc/tech-report
```

and from there run:

```bash
python tools/gen_notation_index.py
python tools/gen_notation_index.py --check
```

The first command regenerates the included table from its sources. The second refuses a stale committed fragment
with a nonzero exit status. Edit the inputs and regenerate; do not repair individual generated cells.
`--check` and `--stats` are mutually exclusive command-line modes. This is a report-tool refusal, not a solver guard.

The selection step in `gen_notation_index.py` is:

```python
first = first_use(symbol_key(r.get("symbol", "")), parts)
```

This excerpt implements step 3 above. It maps text to an index entry; there is no solver equation or timestep attached to it.
The generator implementation is part of the report revision, separate from the solver code pin.[^appa-source]

## Verification and limits

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gen_notation_index.py --check` (report only) | Generated fragment agrees with current inputs | Exact text equality | Generator contract |
| `tools/tests/test_gen_notation_index.py` (pytest, not CTest) | Parsing and index selection fixtures | Exact fixture assertions | Report-tool tests |

: Checks of the notation generator. {#tbl-appa-reader-checks}

[C1] A successful `--check` establishes that the table is current against its inputs.
It does not validate those inputs. [C2] The generator tests exercise the parsing and selection rules;
they do not execute a snapy simulation.[^appa-run]

The generated introduction retains the notation source’s historical revision. Its code-name cells do not certify current-pin implementation behavior. A missing first-use match is a text-search result, not proof that a symbol is unused.

[^appa-source]: Report implementation: `tools/gen_notation_index.py` in the current report revision. Solver claims must be checked separately at `919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274`.

[^appa-run]: Run from the report directory ([How to use and refresh the index](#sec-appa-refresh)) with `python tools/gen_notation_index.py --check` and `PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest -q tools/tests`. The PR evidence records base/head results and Python/pytest versions. These are report checks, with no CPU, CUDA or MPI solver execution claimed.
